title: Isaiah 28
paragraphs: ¹ Woe to the proud crown of Ephraim's drunkards, and to the fading flower of its glorious beauty, which sits on the head of a rich valley — on those who are laid low by wine! ² The Lord has one who is mighty and strong: like a storm of hail and a destroying tempest, like a torrent of rushing floodwaters, he will hurl it to the ground with his hand. ³ The proud crown of Ephraim's drunkards will be trampled underfoot. ⁴ The fading flower of its glorious beauty, set on the head of a fertile valley, will be like a fig that ripens before summer — whoever spots it and picks it swallows it as soon as it is in hand. ⁵ In that day the LORD of hosts will become a glorious crown and a beautiful wreath for the remnant of his people,

⁶ a spirit of justice to the one who sits in judgment, and strength to those who push the battle back to the gate. ⁷ But these leaders also reel with wine and stagger with strong drink — priest and prophet stumble with strong drink, they are confused by wine, they reel with strong drink, they err in vision, they stumble in giving judgment. ⁸ Every table is covered with vomit; not a spot is clean. ⁹ Who is he trying to teach? To whom is he explaining his message? To children just weaned from their milk, to those just taken from the breast? ¹⁰ For it is precept upon precept, precept upon precept, rule upon rule, rule upon rule — a little here, a little there.

¹¹ For through people with strange lips and a foreign tongue the LORD will speak to this people. ¹² He had said to them, "This is the place of rest — give rest to the weary," and "This is the place of repose" — yet they would not listen. ¹³ So the word of the LORD comes to them as precept upon precept, rule upon rule, a little here, a little there — so that they may go stumbling backward, and be broken and snared and taken. ¹⁴ Therefore hear the word of the LORD, you scornful rulers of this people in Jerusalem. ¹⁵ Because you have said, "We have made a covenant with death, and with the grave we have sealed a pact; when the overwhelming disaster sweeps through, it will not reach us — for we have made lies our shelter and falsehood our hiding place."

¹⁶ Therefore thus says the Lord GOD: "Look, I am laying in Zion a stone — a tested stone, a precious cornerstone, a sure foundation. Whoever trusts in it will never be shaken. ¹⁷ I will make justice the measuring line and righteousness the plumb line. Hail will sweep away the shelter of lies, and floodwaters will engulf your hiding place. ¹⁸ Your covenant with death will be annulled, and your pact with the grave will not stand. When the overwhelming disaster sweeps through, you will be beaten down by it. ¹⁹ Whenever it passes through it will take you — morning after morning, by day and by night. The very sight of the news will cause nothing but terror." ²⁰ For the bed is too short to stretch out on, and the blanket too narrow to wrap around oneself.

²¹ For the LORD will rise up as he did at Mount Perazim; he will rouse himself as in the Valley of Gibeon — to do his work, his strange work, and to accomplish his task, his extraordinary task. ²² Now, stop your mockery, or your chains will be made tighter. I have heard from the Lord GOD of hosts the decree of destruction for the whole land. ²³ Listen and hear my voice! Pay attention and hear what I say. ²⁴ Does the farmer plow all day in order to sow? Does he keep breaking up and working the soil? ²⁵ Once he has leveled the surface, does he not scatter dill and spread cumin, and plant wheat in its place, barley in its rows, and spelt in its border?

²⁶ His God teaches him the right way and instructs him. ²⁷ Dill is not threshed with a heavy sledge, nor is a cart wheel rolled over cumin — dill is beaten with a rod and cumin with a stick. ²⁸ Grain for bread is crushed, but not forever — a farmer does not go on threshing it endlessly. He rolls his cart wheel over it, but his horses do not crush it. ²⁹ All this comes from the LORD of hosts — his counsel is wonderful and his wisdom is great.
